title: Outlook for iPhone and iPad: refreshed interface in the Liquid Glass style
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned interface refresh, its default state and the overdue roadmap target without promising a rollout date. The commercial licensing statements match Microsoft's FAQ, and independent searches found no documented switch, separate charge or release requirements specific to this refresh.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe this iOS Liquid Glass refresh at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Outlook" "Liquid Glass"'; opened Outlook mobile release notes and searched Liquid, Glass, redesign, interface, iOS 26: no matches. Search found Mac Liquid Glass documentation, not this iOS refresh.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not published an app build or confirmed rollout date specific to this refresh.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook iOS Liquid Glass refresh minimum version prerequisites roles screens postpone opt out rollout date'; opened Outlook mobile release notes, including November 13, 2026. No build or rollout date identified for this refresh.

claims.quote: Searched: 'Outlook iOS Liquid Glass refresh minimum version prerequisites roles screens postpone opt out rollout date'; opened Outlook mobile release notes, FAQ and Intune configuration page. No user opt-out for this refresh documented.

claims.claim: Outlook for iOS and Android supports general app configuration through Microsoft Intune.
claims.quote: Outlook for iOS and Android supports app settings that allow unified endpoint management (UEM) administrators (using tools such as Microsoft Intune) and Microsoft 365 or Office 365 administrators to customize the behavior of the app.

claims.claim: The cited general configuration tables contain no setting described as controlling this layout or visual redesign.
claims.quote: Searched: Liquid, Glass, redesign, visual, layout, Themes in the opened Intune configuration page; read both general settings tables. Themes covers custom visual themes and beliefs or events, not the app's structural Liquid Glass redesign.
